subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Personalization and Filter Bubbles
description: A micro-lesson that makes Personalization and Filter Bubbles usable.

hook.text: Two people Google the same word and get different results. Algorithms learned their preferences and curated different.

buildup.text: Personalization uses your past behavior to predict what you want next. It increases engagement but narrows your.

discovery.text: Pariser coined filter bubbles: algorithmic curation isolates you in a self-reinforcing loop of similar content.

twist.text: Personalization also drives spending. Targeted ads based on your browsing history can triple conversion rates over.

climax.text: Regularly consume content outside your usual patterns. Browse incognito. Follow opposing viewpoints.

punchline.text: The algorithm shows you who you were, not who you could be.

quiz.question: What is a filter bubble?
options: A security feature that blocks spam content
An algorithmic loop that shows only content matching your past behavior
A browser extension that filters advertisements
